correctness.rationale: Complete intersection smoothness is certified on all five projective charts by the unit Jacobian ideal over F_5. Projective complete-intersection connectedness, adjunction and canonical geometry give a geometrically integral nontrigonal genus-five curve. An independent exact finite verifier checks 31 quadric directions and 781 rational projective points: 27 rank-five, four rank-four with nonsquare discriminants 2,3,3,3, no ranks <=3, and exactly two rational curve points. The published degree-four pencil criterion excludes gonality <=4; a rational point and Riemann–Roch give gonality <=5. Finite enumeration alone is not used as a proof of geometric smoothness.

originality.rationale: The new contribution is an explicit smooth intersection of three quadrics over F_5 with a full arithmetic net-of-quadrics certificate proving gonality five. The motivating 2022 work poses the general existence question and has genus-five realizations only for q<=4; its general genus-five method is stated as a heuristic for other fields. The published 2020 lemma provides a criterion, not the requisite F_5 example. Targeted published source and record searches, together with accessible historical claims, did not uncover an equivalent example. Novelty beyond indexed and accessible materials remains conditional.
residual_risks: An unindexed pre-existing equation or unpublished arithmetic census over F_5 might realize the same existence fact.
Full text of every remotely related source was not inspected; comparison is strongest for the two primary genus-five gonality papers.

value.rationale: The motivating 2022 explicit question asks whether gonality can equal genus over a prescribed finite field. The genus-five q<=4 cases were known, while this small next prime field was not supplied by the inspected studies. The sparse construction resolves the natural pair (g,q)=(5,5) with a direct geometry-plus-arithmetic certificate rather than a cosmetic invariant computation; neither a classification nor a paper-sized extension is claimed.
